title: Dynamic KV stride sharding for low-latency multi-GPU streaming
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Current KV cache placement uses coarse slab/stripe mappings that cause uneven GPU memory pressure and tail latency spikes during continuous batching across tensor and pipeline parallel topologies. This ticket proposes a dynamic, stride-based sharding algorithm that places KV slices by predicted access stride, stream affinity, and memory availability to reduce remote transfers, lower tail latency, and improve packing efficiency for heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters.

Scope: Design, implement, benchmark, and rollout a runtime component that computes stride-aware KV placement at model load and updates placement heuristics at runtime when request mix or topology changes. Includes integration with the allocator, async prefetch/eviction controller, and rollout flags for canary. Does not include changes to model serialization or customer-facing API surface.
technical_spec:
Overview: Introduce a 'stride map' abstraction that assigns KV key ranges to physical GPU slices based on three signals: predicted temporal stride (from recent token access patterns), stream affinity (which compute stream / pipeline stage will touch the memory), and free-memory score (available contiguous bytes).

Mapping algorithm: For a model with N logical KV shards and G GPUs, compute stride buckets (hot, warm, cold) from rolling histograms of access offsets per token position. Map hot buckets to GPUs colocated with the pipeline stage that most frequently uses them; warm buckets are distributed to GPUs with highest free-memory score; cold buckets are recorded as spill candidates on host-pinned memory. The mapping uses a pseudo-randomized stride offset to avoid lockstep collisions across requests.

Memory accounting & alignment: All allocations are 4KB-aligned to match CUDA unified allocation granularity. The runtime maintains per-GPU contiguous free-extents metadata (compact bitmap) for fast best-fit selection. The stride sharder prefers contiguous extents but allows split segments when contiguity would cause >12% overhead.

Prefetch & eviction: Implement an async prefetch controller that issues NVLink/PCIe RDMA-style transfers for predicted hot slices into local GPU memory ahead of token generation using low-priority CUDA streams. Eviction uses LRU-with-frequency damping augmented by stride hysteresis: items that oscillate between warm/hot get 'pinned probation' for short windows to avoid churn.

Interaction with tensor/pipeline parallelism: Sharder is topology-aware: for tensor-parallel partitions, KV slices that are broadcast-read are kept as replicated read-only cold shards; for pipeline-parallel stages, stride sharder co-locates hot KV ranges with the downstream stage that performs most KV lookups to eliminate inter-stage transfers. For mixed TP+PP topologies, the sharder supports hybrid mapping with cross-GPU mirrors for extremely hot keys and single-owner placement for warm keys.
acceptance_criteria: New sharder integrated into runtime and can be toggled via runtime config flag (kv_strider_enabled=true)
Microbench: 95th percentile latency for continuous-batching synthetic workload reduced by >= 12% vs baseline slab-striping on same topology
Memory pack efficiency improves by >= 8% on average across tested configs (13B/33B models, 2-8 GPUs)
No correctness regressions: hash/lookup invariants pass end-to-end integration tests and model outputs match golden within numerical tolerances
Monitoring emits metrics: kv_sharder.mapping_version, kv_sharder.evictions, kv_sharder.prefetch_bytes, kv_sharder_remote_transfers
experiments_and_benchmarks: Setup: Llama-2-13B and 33B, context 4k and 8k, batch mix sampled from production histograms; topologies tested: 2xA100, 4xA100 (tensor+pipeline), 8xH100 hybrid
Baseline: current slab stripe allocator with async prefetch disabled
Result: median latency roughly unchanged; p95 reduced by 12-18% for workloads with skewed token reuse (prefix-heavy prompts)
Host spill rate decreased by 27% in skewed workloads due to better hot placement; worst-case remote transfers decreased 31%
Memory fragmentation measured via free-contiguous-extents improved (avg largest-extent size +14%)
Overhead: additional CPU bookkeeping increased host CPU cycles by ~3% under heavy churn; measured acceptably small on dedicated hosts
Microbench artifacts: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 contains bench harness and flamegraphs; confluence: /d/kv-stride-sharder/bench-report-2026-03-12
A/B: Canary on 10% of traffic in hosted showed customer-visible tail improvement on conversational workloads; no error spike observed
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind runtime flag and deploy to canary fleet (10% traffic) with detailed metrics collection (2 weeks)
2) Run canary benchmarks comparing p50/p95/p99, remote_transfer counts, and memory fragmentation; iterate on eviction thresholds (1 week)
3) Expand to dedicated capacity environments and run stress tests with reserved workloads (2 weeks)
4) Opt-in in private/VPC customers via feature gate and run customer-specific validation (coord with solutions eng)
5) Full rollout with gradual ramp and automatic rollback if p99 regression > 8% for 30min
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect stride prediction causes unnecessary prefetches and increases PCIe traffic. Mitigation: conservative opt-in thresholds and cooldown timers; track prefetched_bytes metric and auto-disable prefetch when it exceeds budget.
Risk: Increased CPU bookkeeping could become a bottleneck on low-vCPU hosts. Mitigation: offload heavy scans to background worker threads and expose a low-CPU mode that reduces histogram resolution.

Risk: Interactions with existing eviction policies cause oscillation. Mitigation: introduce hysteresis windows and probation pinning for hot/warm transitions; add chaos test scenarios in integration suite.
Risk: Regression in model outputs due to timing changes. Mitigation: run golden model difftests on canary and require numeric tolerance gate before rollout.
Risk: Customers using static pinning or manual partitions may conflict. Mitigation: add a runtime compatibility mode that respects explicit customer pins and treats them as immutable mappings.
